name: Training Evaluation Form

scoring.report_note: Report levels in separate lines, never averaged together: item means for reaction, deltas (if a baseline exists) for confidence, raw counts for day-30 behavior. Self-reports without a baseline are labeled 'self-report, no baseline'. Level 4 is out of scope for any form — say so.

timing.distribute: last minutes of final session, in-room

description: A Kirkpatrick-ready evaluation pack for corporate training: 8 reaction items, 3 confidence self-reports (level-2 proxy), 2 keep/change open questions, and a 3-item day-30 follow-up email (level-3 behavior check). Produces a management one-pager.

instructions.when: The reaction items, confidence self-reports and keep/change questions in the last minutes of the final session, in the room. The follow-up by email 30 days later, from the person participants know.
instructions.how: Anonymous. Levels are reported in separate lines, never averaged together — the gap between reaction and behavior is the finding.

items.text: The content matched the work I actually do.
The material went deeper than generalities.
The instructor answered questions with substance.
The materials are ones I will open again.
Exercises took more time than listening.
Sign-up, schedule and room were handled well.
The workload fit alongside my job.
Overall, this training was worth my time.

self_report_items.text: I can apply the main method from this training without help.
I can explain the core idea to a colleague in two minutes.
I know where to look when I get stuck applying it.

open_items.prompt: What worked so well it should stay exactly as it is?
What should change in the next run?

day30_followup.prompt: Since the training, I have used the main method: (never / once / 2-5 times / weekly)
What helped or blocked the using?
What support would make it stick?

report.title: Training Evaluation — management one-pager
sections: Reaction: overall, lowest item by name, highest item by name
Day-30: response count and used-it distribution
Keep and change: one permissioned verbatim each, plus the next-run recommendation
